narrative.overview: CareerPilot CN should resemble a well-organized desk at the moment a candidate makes a consequential decision: the evidence is within reach, the current state is obvious, and the next action is deliberate. The application shell stays restrained so dense qualification, Fact, Campaign, and export information can carry the attention. The interface rejects generic overseas ATS dashboards, flashy startup landing pages, one-click mass apply theater, and resume galleries whose thumbnails are disconnected from real output.
keyCharacteristics: Warm neutral work surface with one burnt-orange action accent.
Compact but readable Chinese-first information hierarchy.
Flat surfaces separated primarily by tone and precise borders.
Real-state feedback for pending, blocked, stale, confirmed, and verified artifacts.
Resume previews may adopt their selected document palette without recoloring the application shell.

rules.name: The One Action Color Rule
rules.body: Burnt orange marks action or current state; it never becomes decorative wallpaper.

rules.name: The Artifact Independence Rule
rules.body: A blue or red resume theme appears inside its preview and export only. It does not recolor Campaign, Fact, or application controls.

rules.name: The Task-Type Rule
rules.body: Inter is mandatory for buttons, inputs, tables, filters, and state labels. Display typography never enters a control.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: A resting card or control uses either a border or a compact shadow, never both as decoration.

dos: Do show the real pending, blocked, stale, confirmed, or verified state beside the affected artifact.
Do render resume thumbnails from the same normalized content model used by DOCX/PDF.
Do keep candidate references private and use anonymous fixtures in shared tests and previews.
donts: Don't imitate generic overseas ATS dashboards that hide decisions behind an unexplained percentage.
Don't use flashy startup landing pages, neon AI gradients, glassmorphism, or decorative automation theater.
Don't present one-click mass apply growth hacks or submission volume as success.
Don't treat social-media resume examples as candidate facts, certified recruiter truth, or verbatim templates.
